assets/vo/s01-e9d40fea.mp3: [excited] What's the difference between zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot prompting? A shot is just an example you put in your prompt. With zero-shot, you give the AI a task and no examples. Say you ask it to rate a customer issue as high, medium, or low priority, and the issue says, I can't access my account, and my report is due today. It will probably say high, but it picks its own format, so one reply might be a single word, and the next might be a whole paragraph. With one-shot, you first show it one example, like a missing password reset email, marked low. Now it copies your format, but it has only seen low, so it has to guess what counts as high. With few-shot, you give it a handful, usually three to five. You add a payment system that's down, marked high, and an invoice question, marked medium. Now it sees your whole scale, so it's much more likely to answer high, and in the same format. Examples make the prompt longer, so start with zero-shot, and add them when the answers aren't consistent. [excited] So zero-shot means no examples, one-shot means one example, and few-shot means a handful. Follow for more AI basics!
